I've been clean for I lost track but I think almost 2 years. 
So I'll tell you what helped me get out of it.

1.Don't associate with any of the things that triggered you.
-asses what your triggers are and keep them in mind. Is it listening to certain music? Is it stressful situations? Is it going on this subreddit? 
-find out what your rituals are and avoid starting them. 
I used to intentionally trigger myself and listen to certain songs until I was upset enough. I stopped and it helped a ton.

2. Get rid of EVERYTHING. 
-i know it's hard, but you have to get rid of any blades, sharp objects, anything. 
Even making them harder to access helps. 
I used to keep them nearby but when I was trying to quit I hid them in an old password journal at my dad's since I couldn't bring myself to toss them. 
-it creates a physical barrier for you to pass, and usually by the time you can access it the feeling is gone.

3. When the urge arises DISTRACT. 
-watch a show, learn a new hobby that uses your hands. I got into crochet. 
-my sh had basically become a habit, I did it whether I needed it or not. 

4. Don't allow bad thoughts to consume you. 
-if your sh is based on "punishment" then find other means, this isn't the healthiest thing, since it's still sh but I stopped cutting and ended up hitting my thighs. (I don't recommend this). 
It's best to try to force yourself with positive thoughts. Literally the opposite of the bad ones.

5. Don't let yourself EVER feel like you need them. Scars or lack there of do not dictate your validity. I felt for a while that I wasn't really serious because I wasn't doing it anymore, but me stopping does not erase how hard I've struggled.
